jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology startup helping freight forwarders turn data into better decisions and measurable business impact. Portcast uses AI to surface shipment exceptions, cost risks, and the right actions, helping teams focus on the shipments that need their attention, keep freight costs under control, and make procurement decisions with confidence. Our vision is to be the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are a lean, globally distributed team building technology for an industry going through a major digital transformation.

About The Role

You'll be the person accountable for the delivery state of our product initiatives once they move into execution. You'll report directly to our Senior Product Manager and make sure ownership is clear across Engineering, Data, and Solutions, work is progressing as expected, dependencies are being managed, and risks are surfaced early rather than when they become launch problems.

We're looking for someone who understands our product, technology, and data well enough to follow the work, understand why we're building something, spot when execution is drifting from the intended outcome, and know when to bring an issue back to Product for clarification.

This is a hands-on IC role and you'll be the first person in this role at Portcast, giving you the opportunity to shape how we manage and deliver product initiatives as we scale. This role requires daily working-hour overlap with our Asia-based Tech Team.

What Success Looks Like In This Role

No launch delays, cleaner releases, and shorter cycle times, driven by earlier identification of risks, dependencies, and blockers, better coordination across Product, Engineering, Data, and Solutions, and clearer visibility into what is moving, what is blocked, and what needs attention.

What You’ll Own

Own delivery from kickoff to release: Take ownership of the operational delivery state once a product initiative moves into execution. Make sure ownership is clear, work starts when expected, progress is visible, and initiatives continue moving through development, testing, and release.
Track dependencies and surface risks early: Monitor cross-functional dependencies, blockers, competing priorities, scope changes, and potential delays.
Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Data, and Solutions: Make sure teams know who owns what, dependencies are understood, and the right people have the context they need. Act as the central point of coordination so Product has a clear view of delivery.
Coordinate handover and launch readiness: Help coordinate the handover between Engineering, Data, Solutions, and Product so that the relevant teams have what they need for testing and acceptance.
Keep execution aligned with product intent: Understand the goals and key requirements behind an initiative well enough to spot when implementation appears to diverge from what was intended. Surface questions, gaps, or inconsistencies early and bring them back to Product for clarification before they become testing or release issues.
Maintain a clear source of truth: Keep tickets, timelines, project status, dependencies, key decisions, and risks up to date so that the team can quickly understand what is moving, what is blocked, and where attention is needed.
Keep delivery moving without creating bureaucracy: Bring structure, follow-through, and accountability to the delivery process without adding unnecessary processes. Join relevant standups and working sessions so you can identify issues and resolve them quickly.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
At least 3+ years in project management, program management, delivery, product operations, or a similar role.
A proven ability to close things and keep initiatives moving: Experience managing projects or initiatives involving multiple technical and cross-functional teams in a startup or B2B SaaS environment, ideally in data-heavy domains, and even better in logistics tech or supply chain tech.
Understands data and strong technical foundation. You can read code, understand how systems and data pipelines fit together, and dig into the work alongside engineers and data scientists. You know the difference between a real blocker and noise.
Strong execution instincts: You naturally keep track of the details that others might miss. You chase loose ends, surface blockers, follow up on dependencies, and make sure decisions actually turn into action.
First-principles problem solving: When something is stuck or going off track, you understand why rather than simply following the existing process. You work out what needs to change and involve the right people to resolve it.
Comfort with ambiguity: You can create clarity when the requirements, ownership, or process aren't fully defined. You are comfortable making progress without having every answer upfront.
Strong cross-functional communication: You can translate between Product, Engineering, Data, and customer-facing teams. You know what different teams need to know, communicate clearly, and escalate issues early without creating unnecessary noise.
High ownership: You don't see your job as simply tracking whether someone completed a task. You take responsibility for the overall delivery state and stay on an issue until it is actually resolved.
Startup mindset: You enjoy working in a lean environment where there isn't a dedicated person for every function. You're willing to get into the details, solve problems yourself, and build lightweight processes when they are genuinely useful.

What’s In It For You

Own a high-leverage problem: You'll be the person responsible for keeping delivery moving across teams, directly influencing how quickly and reliably we turn product ideas into something customers can use.
Work at the intersection of Product, AI, Data, and Logistics: Our products combine software, data, machine learning, and deep logistics expertise. You'll get exposure to complex product problems where the challenge isn't simply building software, but making sure data, models, workflows, and customer needs come together.
Real impact from day one: we’re lean by design so you'll have a high degree of ownership. There is no large PMO or layer of project managers around you. You'll need to be comfortable getting into the details, figuring things out independently, and knowing when something needs to be pushed, clarified, escalated, or simply solved.
Globally distributed, remote-first flexibility: work with a fully distributed team across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration.

OUR CORE VALUES GUIDE EVERYTHING WE DO

Curiosity: We dig into why something's slipping, not just how to patch it. We stay close to the work and the data.
Ownership: We act like founders. We hold a project together end to end and stay on it until it ships cleanly.
Raising the bar: We don't settle for "it launched." We aim for delivery that's predictable, aligned, and free of last-minute surprises.
Effective: We focus on shipping what was actually intended, on time, with real impact, not process for its own sake.

Join us at Portcast in our vision to become the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Job Description Summary

The Field Services Project Manager (FSPM) is responsible for Project Management, Costing, Planning, Coordination and Execution along with supporting Proposal Development and Contract Negotiation of a Nuclear Field Services Project. Execution will be in accordance with to financial/commercial/technical parameters for successful site project execution and customer satisfaction. The role is focused on the execution of site project activities, within an operating discipline covered by standard functional practices and procedures.

Job Description

The Field Services Project Manager (FSPM) is responsible for Project Management, Costing, Planning, Coordination and Execution along with supporting Proposal Development and Contract Negotiation of a Nuclear Field Services Project. Execution will be in accordance with to financial/commercial/technical parameters for successful site project execution and customer satisfaction. The role is focused on the execution of site project activities, within an operating discipline covered by standard functional practices and procedures.

The Project Manager Role Includes

Request opening of projects in ERP System
SME for install/maintenance services during R process.
Attend pre-proposal and negotiation meetings, develop scope and schedule, loadboard, JCE, tooling, quotes, parts, resources, deliverables.
Job Site/Outage planning PRIOR to mobilization.
Generate JIS, Labor and Specialty Service requests.
Coordinate Design Eng. / Customer coord / Pre Site work (T-12, T-6) / Coordinate Lean Outage Risk and Protectivity (LORaP) workshops.
Request internal and external PO’s.
Develop GE OneEHS plan pre-mobilization portion being completed before mobilizing.
Outage Planning: Work order task plans, considering safety requirements, equipment availability, parts on hand, tooling, specialty services and resources.
Ensure Development One EHS plan upon site mobilization prior to outage start.
Development and management of costs with ongoing estimates to completion.
Development, planning and management of the project schedules and payment milestones, while providing contingency planning where required, to ensure a timely execution.
Risk and Opportunity management. Ensuring that all risks and issues are identified, and mitigation plans developed.
Issue resolution during project execution – includes Safety/HOP/Quality/FME/Generate NCR’s/Parts/Product Service/Engineering/Controls/Commercial etc.
To provide accurate management reports of all assigned projects
Ensure all project authorization is secured both technically and financially
To communicate effectively with all the stakeholders, both internal and external.
Manage the Scope Change Authorization process for all assigned projects.
Provide project leadership and guidance from project conception through to project delivery; to the customer and to conduct project feedback reviews at the appropriate time.
It is expected that this position will act as the focus for project-based activities and perform other related duties as assigned or requested
Ensure completion of project field services report, execution of ETC 127 process for engineering documentation of changes, Generate POR Document, Project close out, generate, BP, LL’s and OE summary.
Occasionally, attend training seminars, etc.
Promote GE products in front of customers during presentations and other events, as needed
Maintain excellent relations with customers, peers, Engineering, and global teams

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math) or related technical discipline from an accredited university or college, or 10 years relevant related work experience.
5+ years of relevant project management experience within the power generation or industrial manufacturing industry.
5+ years of relevant commercial and negotiation experience.
Proficient in the English language.
Ability to gain and maintain unescorted access to a Nuclear power facility in Canada, Mexico or the U.S.
Ability to travel, up to 50% annually, within Canada, Mexico, domestically and internationally.
Ability to obtain and maintain a valid passport.
Ability and willingness to work weekends, holidays and overtime as required for the assigned projects.
Ability to walk up to 5 miles a day, climb 3 flights of stairs 3 times a day, and climb ladders as required to access the work areas.

Desired Characteristics

Knowledge of PMP concepts and processes
Experience with Steam Power systems either in a Nuclear, Fossil or Gas power plant setting
Practical knowledge of GE products is a plus but not necessity
Ability to adapt to changing technology
Attention to detail and time management skills to ensure deadlines are met
Clear thinker, detail oriented, insightful, quantitative, and results oriented – Able to make reasoned, sound, and timely decisions
Strong facilitation and presentation skills for technical and business audiences
Able and willing to take ownership and responsibility for assigned tasks
Able to work successfully in a matrix environment, executing multiple assignments and priorities
Continuous improvement “mindset” with an ability to identify, influence, and implement better ways to execute an activity or process
Proficiency in Excel, Word, PowerPoint and working knowledge of Primavera P6
Strong verbal communication skills and customer focused mindset
Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong interpersonal and leadership skills

Additional Information

GE Vernova offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Vernova is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE Vernova will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

Relocation Assistance Provided:
No

This is a remote position

For candidates applying to a U.S. based position, the pay range for this position is between $104,200.00 and $173,700.00. The Company pays a geographic differential of 110%, 120% or 130% of salary in certain areas. jobs.title: IT Project Manager
jobs.description:
Uw rol

Als IT-projectleider verzeker je de realisatie van maatschappelijk relevante ICT-projecten rekening houdend met de planning en de vereiste kwaliteit.

Tevens verzorg je op een regelmatige basis de rapportering over de vooruitgang van de projecten en waak je over een goede communicatie tussen de verschillende betrokken partijen.

Je volgt de activiteiten op en ziet toe op de goede organisatie van het werk binnen de afdeling (operationeel plan, processen en procedures).

Daarnaast organiseer je het change-managementproces en ondersteun je de ontwikkeling en evolutie van de 'Best practices' binnen de afdeling.

Je neemt een motiverende, adviserende en faciliterende rol aan ten aanzien van het management en de business units en werkt nauw met hen samen.

Verder zorg je voor een goed people management waarbij je de betrokken medewerkers stimuleert, coördineert en motiveert tijdens de realisatie van de projecten.

Uw profiel

Je hebt een bachelor- of masterdiploma behaald, bij voorkeur in ICT, en beschikt over minimum 5 jaar ervaring in het beheer van ontwikkelingsprojecten.
Je hebt een goede kennis van analysetechnieken en methodologieën zoals Agile en Prince 2.
Een technische background in de volgende technologieën is een troef: Java, JEE, Openshift, Rest Web Services, .Net...
Je hebt verantwoordelijkheidszin en bent klant- en resultaatgericht.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Research Operations
jobs.description:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews.

Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.

The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.

Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures.

The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people.

We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.

Participant recruitment at Outset spans a global partner network, internal process, and the product experience itself — and this role owns all three. Rather than running recruitment study by study, you'll build the system that makes it predictable at scale. You'll be Outset's authority on recruitment: the connective tissue between our partners, our teams, and our product.

Responsibilities

Own partner performance and communication, with a system to assess and continually optimize each partner's quality, reliability, and best-fit use cases.
Negotiate preferred rates and commercial terms, and build the feasibility process (incidence rates, targeting, which vendor for which use case) that keeps recruitment predictable as volume grows.
Design and document the end-to-end recruitment process, from intake through delivery — with fill-time benchmarks by audience/screening criteria and a clear playbook for tracking and escalating at-risk projects.
Build the internal enablement and training that gets the GTM team up to speed and confident in how recruitment works.
Partner with Product and Engineering on the recruitment experience — fraud detection, identity verification, quality flagging, refunds — bringing structured, evidence-backed problems into the product roadmap.
Identify and spec internal tooling that reduces manual ops work.
Translate how recruitment works into content for two audiences: best-practice guidance for Account Directors/AEs, and customer-facing explanations of our role, our partners' role, and what to expect.

Qualifications

5–10 years in research operations, participant recruitment, or panel/vendor management, with deep expertise in digital qualitative recruitment; experience with quantitative recruitment is a plus
Hands-on understanding of how participant recruitment actually works: panels and marketplaces, screeners, incidence and feasibility, soft launches, quotas, incentives, fraud, and quality control.
Track record managing vendors and partners — selecting, negotiating, holding accountable, managing spend.
Genuine program management ability — you can hold a messy, cross-functional problem in your head, sequence it, and drive it to a working system.
Experience at both a large organization and a startup. We want the enterprise process instincts and the scrappiness to build fast without waiting for permission.
Strong communicator — able to distill complex, cross-functional information into clear training, documentation, playbooks, and customer-facing content.
Comfortable with AI tooling for content and automation; experience building AI tooling/dashboards a plus.
Highly independent — this role is built for someone who defines priorities as much as executes them.
Bonus: experience at a research platform, panel provider, or research agency.

Compensation Range: $150K - $200K

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology startup helping freight forwarders turn data into better decisions and measurable business impact. Portcast uses AI to surface shipment exceptions, cost risks, and the right actions, helping teams focus on the shipments that need their attention, keep freight costs under control, and make procurement decisions with confidence. Our vision is to be the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are a lean, globally distributed team building technology for an industry going through a major digital transformation.

About The Role

You'll be the person accountable for the delivery state of our product initiatives once they move into execution. You'll report directly to our Senior Product Manager and make sure ownership is clear across Engineering, Data, and Solutions, work is progressing as expected, dependencies are being managed, and risks are surfaced early rather than when they become launch problems.

We're looking for someone who understands our product, technology, and data well enough to follow the work, understand why we're building something, spot when execution is drifting from the intended outcome, and know when to bring an issue back to Product for clarification.

This is a hands-on IC role and you'll be the first person in this role at Portcast, giving you the opportunity to shape how we manage and deliver product initiatives as we scale. This role requires daily working-hour overlap with our Asia-based Tech Team.

What Success Looks Like In This Role

No launch delays, cleaner releases, and shorter cycle times, driven by earlier identification of risks, dependencies, and blockers, better coordination across Product, Engineering, Data, and Solutions, and clearer visibility into what is moving, what is blocked, and what needs attention.

What You’ll Own

Own delivery from kickoff to release: Take ownership of the operational delivery state once a product initiative moves into execution. Make sure ownership is clear, work starts when expected, progress is visible, and initiatives continue moving through development, testing, and release.
Track dependencies and surface risks early: Monitor cross-functional dependencies, blockers, competing priorities, scope changes, and potential delays.
Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Data, and Solutions: Make sure teams know who owns what, dependencies are understood, and the right people have the context they need. Act as the central point of coordination so Product has a clear view of delivery.
Coordinate handover and launch readiness: Help coordinate the handover between Engineering, Data, Solutions, and Product so that the relevant teams have what they need for testing and acceptance.
Keep execution aligned with product intent: Understand the goals and key requirements behind an initiative well enough to spot when implementation appears to diverge from what was intended. Surface questions, gaps, or inconsistencies early and bring them back to Product for clarification before they become testing or release issues.
Maintain a clear source of truth: Keep tickets, timelines, project status, dependencies, key decisions, and risks up to date so that the team can quickly understand what is moving, what is blocked, and where attention is needed.
Keep delivery moving without creating bureaucracy: Bring structure, follow-through, and accountability to the delivery process without adding unnecessary processes. Join relevant standups and working sessions so you can identify issues and resolve them quickly.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
At least 3+ years in project management, program management, delivery, product operations, or a similar role.
A proven ability to close things and keep initiatives moving: Experience managing projects or initiatives involving multiple technical and cross-functional teams in a startup or B2B SaaS environment, ideally in data-heavy domains, and even better in logistics tech or supply chain tech.
Understands data and strong technical foundation. You can read code, understand how systems and data pipelines fit together, and dig into the work alongside engineers and data scientists. You know the difference between a real blocker and noise.
Strong execution instincts: You naturally keep track of the details that others might miss. You chase loose ends, surface blockers, follow up on dependencies, and make sure decisions actually turn into action.
First-principles problem solving: When something is stuck or going off track, you understand why rather than simply following the existing process. You work out what needs to change and involve the right people to resolve it.
Comfort with ambiguity: You can create clarity when the requirements, ownership, or process aren't fully defined. You are comfortable making progress without having every answer upfront.
Strong cross-functional communication: You can translate between Product, Engineering, Data, and customer-facing teams. You know what different teams need to know, communicate clearly, and escalate issues early without creating unnecessary noise.
High ownership: You don't see your job as simply tracking whether someone completed a task. You take responsibility for the overall delivery state and stay on an issue until it is actually resolved.
Startup mindset: You enjoy working in a lean environment where there isn't a dedicated person for every function. You're willing to get into the details, solve problems yourself, and build lightweight processes when they are genuinely useful.

What’s In It For You

Own a high-leverage problem: You'll be the person responsible for keeping delivery moving across teams, directly influencing how quickly and reliably we turn product ideas into something customers can use.
Work at the intersection of Product, AI, Data, and Logistics: Our products combine software, data, machine learning, and deep logistics expertise. You'll get exposure to complex product problems where the challenge isn't simply building software, but making sure data, models, workflows, and customer needs come together.
Real impact from day one: we’re lean by design so you'll have a high degree of ownership. There is no large PMO or layer of project managers around you. You'll need to be comfortable getting into the details, figuring things out independently, and knowing when something needs to be pushed, clarified, escalated, or simply solved.
Globally distributed, remote-first flexibility: work with a fully distributed team across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration.

OUR CORE VALUES GUIDE EVERYTHING WE DO

Curiosity: We dig into why something's slipping, not just how to patch it. We stay close to the work and the data.
Ownership: We act like founders. We hold a project together end to end and stay on it until it ships cleanly.
Raising the bar: We don't settle for "it launched." We aim for delivery that's predictable, aligned, and free of last-minute surprises.
Effective: We focus on shipping what was actually intended, on time, with real impact, not process for its own sake.

Join us at Portcast in our vision to become the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.description:
DEPT OF HEALTH SERVICES

The Arizona Department of Health Services promotes and protects the health of Arizona’s children and adults. Our mission is to promote, protect, and improve the health and wellness of individuals and communities in Arizona. We strive to set the standard for personal and community health through direct care, science, public policy, and leadership. ADHS promotes alternative work schedules, flexible hours. We have positions that can fit any stage in your career, from entry to senior level. We offer a robust benefit package, including the ADHS Student Loan Assistance Program, where eligible employees can receive up to $300.00 per month for their outstanding student loans. Come check us out and see how you can make a difference in the lives of all Arizonans.

Program Manager, Environmental Public Health Tracking

Job Location:

Address: 150 N 18th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85007

Posting Details

Salary: $82,500

Grade: 24

*Hybrid*

Job Summary

This position will oversee the Environmental Public Health Tracking program within the Office of Environmental Epidemiology and is responsible for overall management and supervision of the program and any assigned personnel. This position performs supervisory and advanced professional analytical work related to environmental public health tracking, data analysis, reporting, visualization, and dissemination. Supervises and directs the work activities of subordinate staff involved in environmental public health tracking activities, including the acquisition and integration of environmental and public health data from multiple sources. Reviews and conducts literature reviews and data analyses to support program activities and public health practices. Provide training and technical support to program staff and data users as needed. Reviews work products or achievements of subordinate workers; evaluates work and formulates plans for improvements. Oversees implementation of program procedures, data management practices, and operational activities to support the program activities. Collaborates with the GIS and IT teams to support tracking activities. Collaborates with communities, partners, and stakeholders to support the use and understanding of environmental public health data and tracking resources. Participates in after-hours activities, including partner meetings and emergency response as needed. Participates in writing grants, other funding proposals, and grant reports.

Job Duties

Oversee, manage, and supervise the work of epidemiologists and associated staff conducting Environmental Public Health Tracking activities. Plans, assigns, schedules, prioritizes, directs, and coordinates the work of assigned epidemiologists and other staff.

Leads and manages the Environmental Public Health Tracking Program, including program planning, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement activities. Oversees the acquisitions and integration of environmental and public health data from multiple sources to support program activities and inform public health practice.

Oversees implementation of program procedures, data management practices, and operational activities. Collaborates with GIS and IT teams to support tracking activities, data resources, and program needs.

Provides training, guidance, and technical support to program staff and data users.

Collaborates with communities, partners, and stakeholders to support the use and understanding of environmental public health data and tracking resources.

Participates in after-hours activities, including partner meetings and emergency response as needed. Participates in writing grants, other funding proposals, and grant reports.

Other duties as assigned as related to the position.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities (KSAs):

Knowledge Of:

Considerable independent judgment and advanced knowledge of applied epidemiology for public health practice.
Managerial techniques and personnel policies and procedures.
Contemporary principles and practices of epidemiology.
Principles and practices applicable to the control and prevention of diseases.
Methods, procedures and techniques used in developing, implementing, and maintaining disease surveillance and control programs.
Contemporary medical methods and practices used in the control of a variety of diseases.
Program planning and fiscal monitoring practices and procedures.
Performance Management (PM), and Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) and Lean methodologies.

Skills In

Working management and work leadership.
Oral and written communication.
Interpersonal relations, as applied to contracts with representatives of other governmental and private organizations, physicians, and the public.
Conducting scientific studies and investigations required to identify and isolate various diseases.
Supervision, program planning and administration, contract/budget monitoring, and grant writing.
Public health surveillance, computerized database management, data analysis, program evaluation, literature search, effective verbal and written communication, and interpersonal skills.

Ability To

Support a diverse multi-cultural workforce that reflects the community, promotes equal opportunity at all levels of public employment, and creates an inclusive work environment that enables all individuals to perform to their fullest potential free from discrimination.

Selective Preference(s)

Masters of public health in Epidemiology and two years of professional experience in public health agency. One year of management/supervisory duties. Ideal candidate will have experience using statistical software (e.g. SAS programming), working with the different levels of US health care system and public health system, and working with electronic public health surveillance databases.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology startup helping freight forwarders turn data into better decisions and measurable business impact. Portcast uses AI to surface shipment exceptions, cost risks, and the right actions, helping teams focus on the shipments that need their attention, keep freight costs under control, and make procurement decisions with confidence. Our vision is to be the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are a lean, globally distributed team building technology for an industry going through a major digital transformation.

About The Role

You'll be the person accountable for the delivery state of our product initiatives once they move into execution. You'll report directly to our Senior Product Manager and make sure ownership is clear across Engineering, Data, and Solutions, work is progressing as expected, dependencies are being managed, and risks are surfaced early rather than when they become launch problems.

We're looking for someone who understands our product, technology, and data well enough to follow the work, understand why we're building something, spot when execution is drifting from the intended outcome, and know when to bring an issue back to Product for clarification.

This is a hands-on IC role and you'll be the first person in this role at Portcast, giving you the opportunity to shape how we manage and deliver product initiatives as we scale. This role requires daily working-hour overlap with our Asia-based Tech Team.

What Success Looks Like In This Role

No launch delays, cleaner releases, and shorter cycle times, driven by earlier identification of risks, dependencies, and blockers, better coordination across Product, Engineering, Data, and Solutions, and clearer visibility into what is moving, what is blocked, and what needs attention.

What You’ll Own

Own delivery from kickoff to release: Take ownership of the operational delivery state once a product initiative moves into execution. Make sure ownership is clear, work starts when expected, progress is visible, and initiatives continue moving through development, testing, and release.
Track dependencies and surface risks early: Monitor cross-functional dependencies, blockers, competing priorities, scope changes, and potential delays.
Coordinate across Product, Engineering, Data, and Solutions: Make sure teams know who owns what, dependencies are understood, and the right people have the context they need. Act as the central point of coordination so Product has a clear view of delivery.
Coordinate handover and launch readiness: Help coordinate the handover between Engineering, Data, Solutions, and Product so that the relevant teams have what they need for testing and acceptance.
Keep execution aligned with product intent: Understand the goals and key requirements behind an initiative well enough to spot when implementation appears to diverge from what was intended. Surface questions, gaps, or inconsistencies early and bring them back to Product for clarification before they become testing or release issues.
Maintain a clear source of truth: Keep tickets, timelines, project status, dependencies, key decisions, and risks up to date so that the team can quickly understand what is moving, what is blocked, and where attention is needed.
Keep delivery moving without creating bureaucracy: Bring structure, follow-through, and accountability to the delivery process without adding unnecessary processes. Join relevant standups and working sessions so you can identify issues and resolve them quickly.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
At least 3+ years in project management, program management, delivery, product operations, or a similar role.
A proven ability to close things and keep initiatives moving: Experience managing projects or initiatives involving multiple technical and cross-functional teams in a startup or B2B SaaS environment, ideally in data-heavy domains, and even better in logistics tech or supply chain tech.
Understands data and strong technical foundation. You can read code, understand how systems and data pipelines fit together, and dig into the work alongside engineers and data scientists. You know the difference between a real blocker and noise.
Strong execution instincts: You naturally keep track of the details that others might miss. You chase loose ends, surface blockers, follow up on dependencies, and make sure decisions actually turn into action.
First-principles problem solving: When something is stuck or going off track, you understand why rather than simply following the existing process. You work out what needs to change and involve the right people to resolve it.
Comfort with ambiguity: You can create clarity when the requirements, ownership, or process aren't fully defined. You are comfortable making progress without having every answer upfront.
Strong cross-functional communication: You can translate between Product, Engineering, Data, and customer-facing teams. You know what different teams need to know, communicate clearly, and escalate issues early without creating unnecessary noise.
High ownership: You don't see your job as simply tracking whether someone completed a task. You take responsibility for the overall delivery state and stay on an issue until it is actually resolved.
Startup mindset: You enjoy working in a lean environment where there isn't a dedicated person for every function. You're willing to get into the details, solve problems yourself, and build lightweight processes when they are genuinely useful.

What’s In It For You

Own a high-leverage problem: You'll be the person responsible for keeping delivery moving across teams, directly influencing how quickly and reliably we turn product ideas into something customers can use.
Work at the intersection of Product, AI, Data, and Logistics: Our products combine software, data, machine learning, and deep logistics expertise. You'll get exposure to complex product problems where the challenge isn't simply building software, but making sure data, models, workflows, and customer needs come together.
Real impact from day one: we’re lean by design so you'll have a high degree of ownership. There is no large PMO or layer of project managers around you. You'll need to be comfortable getting into the details, figuring things out independently, and knowing when something needs to be pushed, clarified, escalated, or simply solved.
Globally distributed, remote-first flexibility: work with a fully distributed team across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration.

OUR CORE VALUES GUIDE EVERYTHING WE DO

Curiosity: We dig into why something's slipping, not just how to patch it. We stay close to the work and the data.
Ownership: We act like founders. We hold a project together end to end and stay on it until it ships cleanly.
Raising the bar: We don't settle for "it launched." We aim for delivery that's predictable, aligned, and free of last-minute surprises.
Effective: We focus on shipping what was actually intended, on time, with real impact, not process for its own sake.

Join us at Portcast in our vision to become the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

As a member of our corporate security team, the Manager – Business Resiliency and Security Operations will be responsible for leading mature, enterprise-wide programs spanning crisis management, emergency response, emergency preparedness, training, and critical-event technology developing. This includes but is not limited to emergency response processes/procedure, crisis management processes/procedures, site threat assessments, ER/CM planning, exercises, automating processes (where possible), employee training programs, etc. The position will also coordinate with event security, travel security, executive protection and administer industry and government/industry regulated security programs (e.g., ISO, OSHA, etc.); while establishing and conducting audit processes with various partners, functional areas, Safety, Security Systems Integration, and Physical Security, to pressure test processes and meet customer (internal and external) requirements.

Crisis Management and Critical Event Operations: Own and continuously improve the enterprise crisis management framework, including plans, playbooks, governance, activation protocols, executive support, after-action reviews, and lessons learned. Emergency Response and Site Readiness: Develop and standardize emergency response capabilities and Emergency Action Plans across sites. Emergency Preparedness and Employee Engagement: Build a proactive culture of readiness through timely preparedness content, employee resources, newsletters, awareness campaigns, exercises, and engagement events. Plan exercises that pressure-test plans, systems, and decision-making, then convert findings into accountable improvement actions.
Gather and analyze data and make recommendations on operational improvements and risk mitigation to business units. Support efforts in Intelligence, GSOC, Travel Security, Event Security, and Executive Protection programs.

Brief Description

Company Overview

ARA is a leading C5ISR company that designs, manufactures, tests and installs innovative technologies that provide the national security community with unparalleled situational awareness, threat detection, and communications capabilities.

Our disruptive, integrated solutions, assemblies and subsystems rise to the challenging demands of discerning, mission-critical customers.

We leverage our capabilities to meet and exceed the requirements of our customers and empower them to remain ahead of evolving threats and complexities in a dynamic security landscape.

Job Summary

We are seeking a Sr. Program Manager responsible for planning and overseeing one or more programs to achieve quality, cost, schedule, technical, and contractual objectives.

The Sr. Program Manager leads program execution, manages resources and risks, monitors performance, and provides customer and leadership updates throughout the program lifecycle.

The Sr. Program Manager will lead the development, production, delivery, and sustainment of RF components, subsystems, and systems supporting mission-critical customers.

This position will lead military SATCOM programs supporting the Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and Global Broadcast Service (GBS) missions and will work closely with the Department of War, U.S. Space Force, and other government customers.

The ideal candidate is a technically capable program leader who can translate customer requirements into clear directions, drive cross-functional execution, and build strong customer relationships.

Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Support and/or lead capture, bid, and proposal activities.
Manage and direct the daily execution of multiple programs or large-scale programs within contract requirements to ensure that cost, schedule, and performance goals are met.
Lead all meetings and the Integrated Product Team from proposal kickoff through program close.
Provide interface, communication, and coordination with internal and external customers on matters pertaining to existing contracts and bid and proposal activities.
Serve as a primary customer interface with Department of War, U.S. Space Force, other government organizations, prime contractors, and external stakeholders.
Represent management at program reviews, meetings, seminars, and other program-related events.
Develop and implement plans and schedules to execute contracts/subcontracts.
Allocate and control contract budgets for labor, material, travel, and purchased services.
Report program status to senior management.
Formally identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate risk throughout the program lifecycle.
Perform variance analysis of schedule and cost on a formal and informal basis and present them to senior management.
Assure that contractual requirements are executed in accordance with applicable regulatory and Company policies and procedures.
Demonstrate the ability to manage changing priorities and aggressive timelines.
Lead company program reviews due to knowledge and experience.

Position Qualifications

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

Competency Statement (s)

Adaptability - Adapts to change, open to new ideas and responsibilities
Communication – Ability to communicate thoughts clearly, both oral and written in a honest, open and timely manner
Job Knowledge - Understands facets of job, aware of duties and responsibilities, keeps job knowledge current
Technical Skill - Possesses the knowledge and skills needed to perform a job or role effectively
Dependability - Meets deadlines, works independently or in a team environment, is accountable, maintains focus, good attendance record
Quality - Strives to eliminate errors, accurate work is a priority, seeks opportunities to improve products
Ethics - Honest, accountable, maintains confidentiality Initiative/Take Ownership – Takes action, seeks new opportunities, strives to see projects to completion, meaning own your job and see it through
Decision Making - Problem solve and critical thinking skills, be able to reach a decision, takes thoughtful approach when considering options, seek input from others, makes difficult decisions
Customer Focus - Understands and can meet the needs in a customer-centric (Internal and External) environment and build strong relationships. Promotes a positive image of the company and strives to solve issues raised by customers
Results Driven - Defines appropriate goals, works toward achieving goals, articulates vision and steps for achievement.

Experience And Skills

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

Active U.S. Secret security clearance required 10-15 years of program management or related experience.
Experience managing programs with responsibility for cost, schedule, risk, and contractual deliverables.
Experience managing firm fixed-price and cost-type contracts.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and Integrated Product Teams.
Experience working with commercial and government customers.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Microsoft Project.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Experience

Experience managing Department of War programs or programs of record, preferably supporting the U.S. Space Force.
Experience with military SATCOM, preferably WGS and GBS, or related communications systems. Working knowledge of GEO satellite communications, ground terminals, RF systems, or related technologies.
Experience with system sustainment, configuration management, field support, obsolescence management, or technology refresh. PMP certification.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field required

jobs.description:
Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

The purpose of the Project Manager position is to plan and coordinate projects to meet the overall goals of the project and serve as the main contact with the contractor or owner.

Essential Job Duties

Review shop drawings, contract drawings, specifications, and applicable standards to determine appropriate installation methods.
Generate proposals for change orders, and as assigned.
Determine labor requirements and preparing schedules, track changes.
Order and track material, equipment, tools, and other necessary items based on design and/or contract needs.
Review time for assigned projects and/or contracts to ensure alignment with project budget.
Monitor overall progress of the project and preparing job records
Generate proposals for change orders, RFI’s, ASI’s and MCR’s; communicate approved items into organizational system(s) and/or to designated representative for processing.
Ensure employees follow all relevant safety standards and procedures, work environment in accordance with the SFP standards.
Meet with AHJ’s, contractors, owners, architects, and other design professionals on project progress.
Perform a formal project review with the Fire Alarm Manager weekly, or as requested.
Assist support staff and facilitate closeout documents to include O&Ms and review as-built drawings for accuracy.
Other duties may be assigned.

Qualifications

The qualifications listed below are representative of the elements required to perform the job successfully, however in some cases, an equivalent combination of Education, Training, Certifications and Experience may meet the job qualifications.

Education, Training, Certifications

High School diploma, technical or related experience and/or training, required.
NICET III ITM Water based systems and/or NICET Level IV Fire Alarm, preferred.

Experience, Knowledge, Skill Requirements

5 years’ industry experience, required.
Successful experience in leading multiple projects, achieving goaled outcomes including profitability while communicating with onsite customers, preferred.
Mechanical aptitude, preferred.
Basic and advanced math skills, required.

Communication Skills

Must have the ability to effectively read, write and communicate in English with employees and customers.

Systems And Software Skills

Ability to operate a computer, use Microsoft Office required.

Other Qualifications

Valid driver’s license with acceptable driving record required.
Must be able to comply with SFS’s Drug and Alcohol policy and Background screening requirements, which may also include customer specific requirements based on contractual agreement.

Physical & Work Environment Requirements

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform Essential Job Duties.

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to sit for long periods. Employee will occasionally be required to bend, kneel, balance, lift <20lb, walk, stand, ascend/descend stairs, drive, twist, and reach above and below shoulders. jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Role Summary

The Project Manager oversees multiple mechanical construction projects in the Gatineau area, managing budgets, schedules, and resources to ensure successful delivery. This role works closely with foremen, subcontractors, and vendors to achieve financial and operational goals while maintaining strong client relationships.

Why This Role Matters to Modern Niagara

Project Managers are key to delivering safe, on-time, and on-budget projects. Their leadership ensures client satisfaction, profitability, and alignment with Modern Niagara’s standards, supporting long-term growth and repeat business.

Key Impact / Purpose

Manage project budgets, schedules, and resources to achieve financial targets.
Build and maintain strong client relationships while promoting Modern Niagara’s full-service offerings.
Ensure safety and quality standards are upheld throughout project execution.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Build project budgets, procure equipment and subcontractors, and manage billing and collections.
Participate in estimating turnover, pre-construction, and post-construction meetings.
Complete monthly financial forecasting and attend project status reviews.
Attend client and construction meetings; communicate updates to teams and subcontractors.
Manage and coordinate equipment and systems commissioning.
Review contracts and determine project scope during pre-construction.
Maintain safety standards across all project activities.
Prepare and update WIP forecast sheets monthly.
Conduct job site progress walks and monitor construction status.
Create purchase orders for suppliers and subcontractors.
Break out labor budgets and review with foremen; monitor labor progress and make financial decisions as needed.

Must-haves:

Post-secondary degree in Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent experience.
Must be eligible to obtain Government Reliability Security Clearance.
5+ years of experience as a Mechanical Project Manager in construction.
Ability to read and interpret mechanical construction drawings and documents.
Strong understanding of construction processes, costs, and budgets.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and scheduling software.
Ability to plan and manage project schedules effectively.
Knowledge of basic accounting principles (asset).
Ability to work in both office and field environments with high interaction across teams.

Nice-to-haves:

Experience overseeing manufacturing project lifecycles.
Strong financial acumen and decision-making skills.

This is a new position. Expected annual compensation; $90,000 - $115,000.

Modern Niagara offers a competitive total compensation package including:

Performance based bonus opportunities.
Defined Contribution Pension Plan with a generous employer contribution.
Flexible Health and Dental benefits with tiered options to meet the needs of you and your family.
An annual health spending account to support your overall wellness.
24/7 confidential support through our Employee and Family Assistance Program with access to comprehensive resources and professional services.
A competitive vacation package with additional vacation granted throughout your tenure with the organization.
Employer Paid Parental Leave Top Up.
Annual Community Day dedicated to volunteering and giving back to the communities where we live and work.
Corporate Discounts through various vendors across Canada for programs such as fitness, mobile phones, travel, home and auto insurance and many others.
Here at Modern Niagara, because we know our people are the best in the industry, we pride ourselves on providing a total compensation package that rewards employees for their hard work and supports employees and their families in their overall wellbeing.

About Modern Niagara

Who We Are

Modern Niagara helps building owners, managers, and general contractors meet the mechanical, electrical, integrated building technology, and building services needs of their buildings across Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Toronto, Southwestern Ontario, and Ottawa. We are committed to having a positive and meaningful impact on Canada’s infrastructure — and on the communities where we live, learn, work, and heal. We build for life.

Our Culture & Values

We value passion, initiative, determination, professionalism, and teamwork. Health and safety are embedded in everything we do, and our award-winning safety culture consistently performs well above industry standards.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Modern Niagara

We are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive organization where everyone has access to opportunity, feels a sense of belonging, and can thrive. We actively work to remove barriers faced by members of equity-seeking groups (including women, Indigenous, Black, racialized, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, people with disabilities, and newcomers to Canada) in the construction industry. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and lived experiences and are committed to a barrier-free hiring process.

If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us at careers@modernniagara.com so we can make appropriate arrangements.

We appreciate every applicant’s interest in joining Modern Niagara. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Résumé du poste

Le gestionnaire de projet est responsable de la supervision de multiples projets de construction mécanique dans la région de Gatineau. Il gère les budgets, les échéanciers et les ressources afin d'assurer la réalisation réussie des projets. Ce rôle travaille en étroite collaboration avec les contremaîtres, les sous-traitants et les fournisseurs afin d'atteindre les objectifs financiers et opérationnels tout en maintenant de solides relations avec les clients.

Pourquoi ce poste est important chez Modern Niagara

Les gestionnaires de projet jouent un rôle clé dans la réalisation de projets sécuritaires, rentables et livrés dans les délais. Leur leadership contribue à la satisfaction des clients, à la rentabilité des projets et au respect des standards de Modern Niagara, favorisant ainsi la croissance à long terme et le développement de relations d'affaires durables.

Impact et objectif du poste

Gérer les budgets, les échéanciers et les ressources des projets afin d'atteindre les objectifs financiers.
Développer et maintenir de solides relations avec les clients tout en promouvant l'ensemble des services offerts par Modern Niagara.
Veiller au respect des normes de santé, sécurité et qualité tout au long de l'exécution des projets.

Responsabilités principales:

Élaborer les budgets de projets, effectuer l'approvisionnement des équipements et des sous-traitants, et gérer la facturation ainsi que les recouvrements.
Participer aux réunions de transfert de soumission, de préconstruction et de post-construction.
Réaliser les prévisions financières mensuelles et participer aux revues d'avancement des projets.
Assister aux réunions de chantier et aux rencontres avec les clients, puis communiquer les mises à jour aux équipes et sous-traitants.
Gérer et coordonner la mise en service des équipements et des systèmes.
Réviser les contrats et définir la portée des travaux pendant la phase de préconstruction.
Maintenir les normes de santé et sécurité pour l'ensemble des activités des projets.
Préparer et mettre à jour mensuellement les prévisions de travaux en cours (WIP).
Effectuer des visites de chantier afin de suivre l'avancement des travaux.
Créer les bons de commande pour les fournisseurs et sous-traitants.
Répartir les budgets de main-d'œuvre, les réviser avec les contremaîtres, suivre l'avancement des travaux et prendre les décisions financières nécessaires.

Qualifications requises:

Diplôme postsecondaire en gestion de la construction, en génie mécanique ou expérience équivalente.
Admissibilité à l'obtention d'une cote de sécurité de niveau Fiabilité du gouvernement du Canada.
Minimum de cinq (5) années d'expérience à titre de gestionnaire de projet mécanique dans l'industrie de la construction.
Capacité à lire et interpréter des plans et documents de construction mécanique.
Bonne compréhension des processus de construction, des coûts et de la gestion budgétaire.
Maîtrise de Microsoft Office et de logiciels de planification.
Capacité à élaborer et gérer efficacement les échéanciers de projets.
Connaissance des principes de base en comptabilité (atout).
Capacité à travailler autant au bureau que sur les chantiers et à collaborer avec plusieurs intervenants.

Atouts:

Expérience de gestion de projets manufacturiers. Solides compétences en analyse financière et en prise de décision.

Il s'agit d'un remplacement de poste. La rémunération annuelle prévue se situe entre 90 000 $ et 115 000 $.

Ce que Modern Niagara vous offre

Modern Niagara offre un programme de rémunération globale concurrentiel comprenant :

Régime de retraite à cotisation déterminée avec une généreuse contribution de l’employeur.
Programme flexible d’assurance maladie et dentaire avec plusieurs niveaux de couverture pour répondre aux besoins de vous et de votre famille.
Compte annuel de dépenses santé pour soutenir votre bien-être global.
Programme d’aide aux employés et à leur famille disponible 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, offrant un accès confidentiel à de nombreuses ressources et services professionnels.
Programme de vacances concurrentiel avec des jours supplémentaires accordés en fonction de l’ancienneté.
Bonification du congé parental payée par l’employeur.
Journée communautaire annuelle consacrée au bénévolat et à l’implication dans les communautés où nous vivons et travaillons.
Rabais corporatifs offerts partout au Canada sur différents services, notamment les programmes de conditionnement physique, la téléphonie mobile, les voyages, les assurances habitation et automobile et bien plus encore.

Chez Modern Niagara, nous savons que nos employés sont les meilleurs de l’industrie. C’est pourquoi nous sommes fiers d’offrir une rémunération globale qui reconnaît leur contribution et soutient leur bien-être ainsi que celui de leur famille.

À propos de Modern Niagara

Qui sommes-nous?

Modern Niagara aide les propriétaires immobiliers, les gestionnaires d’immeubles et les entrepreneurs généraux à répondre aux besoins en mécanique, électricité, technologies intégrées du bâtiment et services aux bâtiments partout au Canada, notamment à Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Toronto, dans le sud-ouest de l’Ontario et à Ottawa. Nous nous engageons à avoir un impact positif et significatif sur les infrastructures canadiennes ainsi que sur les communautés où nous vivons, apprenons, travaillons et nous rétablissons. Nous construisons pour la vie.

Notre culture et nos valeurs

Nous valorisons la passion, l’initiative, la détermination, le professionnalisme et le travail d’équipe. La santé et la sécurité sont au cœur de toutes nos activités et notre culture de sécurité primée surpasse constamment les normes de l’industrie.

Diversité, équité et inclusion

Nous nous engageons à bâtir une organisation diversifiée, équitable et inclusive où chacun a accès aux opportunités, ressent un sentiment d’appartenance et peut s’épanouir pleinement.Nous encourageons les candidatures de personnes de tous horizons et de toutes expériences de vie, y compris les femmes, les peuples autochtones, les personnes noires et racisées, les personnes 2SLGBTQIA+, les personnes en situation de handicap et les nouveaux arrivants au Canada.Si vous avez besoin de mesures d’adaptation à quelque étape que ce soit du processus de recrutement, veuillez communiquer avec nous à careers@modernniagara.com afin que nous puissions prendre les dispositions nécessaires.

jobs.description:
Job Description

BlueScope is an Australian-born global success story spanning 15 countries. Our team of over 16,500 people is our strength and we want our people to be safe, successful and well. We’re leaders and innovators in transforming steel into smart products and solutions that support society, today and in the future. We’re proud of brands, like COLORBOND ® steel that inspire and protect everything from hospitals to bridges and stadiums.

The Opportunity

BlueScope Building Components is looking for a Supply Chain Project Manager
to join the National Supply Chain team
. BlueScope Building Components, a division of BlueScope in Australia, manufactures and markets steel building products, solutions and services through its four leading brands: Lysaght, Fielders, Ranbuild and Kiteleys.

In this permanent full-time position
, you will lead a diverse portfolio of strategic and operational projects aimed at creating a more efficient, consistent and future-ready supply chain. From process optimisation and product rationalisation to automation and AI-enabled initiatives, you will help shape how supply chain activities are delivered across our national business.

Working across multiple sites and functions, you will turn complex business challenges into practical solutions that simplify work, strengthen capability and deliver lasting value. This is a hands-on position for someone who can move comfortably between strategic thinking and practical implementation, bringing people together to embed meaningful and sustainable change.

The role can be based in any Australian capital city
, with key BlueScope locations including Emu Plains and Mascot (NSW), Archerfield (QLD) and Lyndhurst (VIC)
. We offer a flexible hybrid working model
, including the opportunity to work from home up to three days per week
. As this is a national role, occasional travel to BlueScope sites across Australia will be required, averaging approximately six trips per year.

What Will You Do?

Working across longer-term transformation initiatives and shorter-term operational improvements, you will collaborate with supply chain, operations, sales and technology teams to deliver meaningful change. You will:

lead national supply chain improvement projects that enhance efficiency, standardise processes and strengthen operational performance
partner with supply chain, operations, sales and technology teams to deliver strategic and operational transformation initiatives
identify opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce manual activities and introduce automation and digital solutions
develop and embed consistent processes, procedures and ways of working across multiple sites
use operational data and insights to identify constraints, prioritise improvements and support informed decision-making
guide projects through implementation, change adoption and post-implementation support to ensure improvements are successfully embedded

More About You

You are a practical and influential project professional who is comfortable moving between strategy and hands-on delivery. You bring structure to ambiguity, build trusted relationships and know how to maintain momentum when outcomes depend on the support of people across different teams, functions and locations. You will bring:

jobs.description:
About Toronto Community Housing Corporation

Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.

Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.

Vacancy Type

Full-time Permanent

Salary/Hourly Range

$123,900.46 - $136,290.51

Work Details (Days/Hours)

Monday – Friday, 36.25 hours per week

Hybrid Eligible

Yes

Affiliation

Non-Union: Management/Exempt

Division and Department

Development

Number Of Vacancies

1

Existing/New Job

Existing

Grade

08

Vacancy Status

Existing Vacancy

Candidate List Or Eligibility List

Candidate List

What We Offer

In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:

Ability to participate in inclusive employee-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
Minimum three (3) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
Four (4) paid personal days;
Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100-per-cent employer matching;
Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
Employee and family assistance program;
Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year.
Fitness membership discount;

This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.

Make a difference

Reporting to the Senior Development Director, the Senior Project Manager, Construction will work in a fast paced environment and interact with stakeholders, government agencies, business partners, community partners, tenants and internal staff to plan, organize, and manage external contractors. Leading external construction teams and professional consultants, the Senior Project Manager, Construction is responsible for overseeing the design and construction of TCHC rental housing projects and acting as the main point of contact with the external contractors. All work is done in coordination with internal teams and in a manner that aligns with TCHC's tenant focused culture.

Senior Project Manager, Constructions will monitor the progress of specific construction projects on cost control, drawing review, coordination, consultation, facilitation and documentation of project development from project design through to construction completion and turnover. Other duties include regular reporting, acting as a professional resource providing expertise in construction management to Senior Development Managers in preparation of preliminary/final budgets, value-engineering throughout projects planning and production drawings, planning of construction sequencing, analysis of activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to determine progress towards completion. Development initiatives consist of a mix of high-rise and low-rise rental, affordable ownership, market ‘for-sale’ housing with commercial retail, office and recreational components. Projects range from $3 Million to $500+ Million in construction value. All current projects are designed with high energy efficiency measures, some projects are to be LEED, Toronto Green Standard, or Energy Star certified.

What You'll Do

The Senior Project Manager, Construction, working with a project team, will oversee all aspects of the project lifecycle from schematic design and construction through to turnover and occupancy. Key responsibilities and essential job functions include but are not limited to the following:

Design & Pre-construction

Manages the design of building schemes and specifications, ensuring alignment with corporate goals, objectives and design standards along with regulatory requirements
Provide input and oversight into consultant’s design with respect to cost, constructability and operational effectiveness
Participate in resident and community meetings and consultations informing the community about the status of design and/or construction and getting feedback on proposed designs
Meet with, and negotiate with neighboring owners regarding various agreements, including pre-construction surveys, tiebacks and craneswing
Manages the preparation of materials and timing for review at the TCHC Design Review Panel as it relates to the different projects
Manages the procurement process for retaining design consultants
Attends design consultant meetings, and reports back to the project team

Construction

Act as the primary contact for TCHC when managing the third-party contactor
Provides management and oversight to the construction schedule and budgets for each project including regular reporting to internal finance and other divisions
Coordinates all administrative aspects of the construction process, including management of consultants, vendors, plan revisions, occupancy date changes, processing of monthly progress draws, etc.
Preparation of RFQs and RFPs for contractors or consultants as required
Acts as a liaison between project sites and various TCHC divisions
Reviews plans and specifications as required
Approves and processes all change orders and investigates discrepancies
Attends site meetings throughout the duration of construction and reports back to the project team
Work with internal and external legal counsel in the preparation of construction management contracts and contract negotiation
Implement controls to mitigate TCHC risk through the course of a project including risks to the budget, schedule and site
Manages the turnover process of new residential units to the internal Asset Management division within TCHC

Financial Accountability

Maintains and tracks project budgets and expenses
Continuously evaluates and recommends value engineering opportunities to improve financial performance of the project
Reporting to the shareholder, executive leadership team and/or the TCHC Board of Directors as required
Leadership
Supervises, mentors and monitors the performance of direct reports
Develops and maintains a high performance team through coaching and development
Identifies areas for improvement among teams and implements processes to achieve high productivity within construction

What You'll Need

Post-secondary education in architecture, engineering, project management or related areas
P.Eng, OAA, , OACETT, or PMP recommended
Knowledge of Ontario Building Code, LEED, Toronto Green Standards, AODA, and Energy Star
Experience negotiating CCDC 5B and 5A contracts is considered an asset
Knowledge of Tarion or Residential Tenancies Act is considered an asset
Minimum 7 years of design, construction and project management experience with demonstrated experience designing and managing construction of multi-unit high-rise residential buildings.
Experience with other types of buildings such as institutional, community centres, retail or commercial is an asset
Experience managing multi-disciplinary teams
Organizational and planning skills, with a demonstrated ability to solve problems and make decisions in a timely manner
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Knowledge of development process life cycle
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings
Negotiation skills
Experience with procurement processes
Must have excellent interpersonal skills and proven track record with managing internal and external stakeholder relations
Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Project) and AutoCAD

What's Next

Once you apply, we’ll review your resume to determine if your skills and experience match the qualifications for the role and only qualified candidates will be contacted for next steps. If you move forward, the process may include an interview, written/practical test, and reference check.

INDS

Thank you for your interest in Toronto Community Housing

We recognize that people bring experience and talent that goes beyond the technical skills and requirements of a job. If you possess similar experience that is close to what we’ve included in the job postings below, we encourage you to consider applying. We strongly believe that diverse experience, transferable skills, and passion are key!

Once you have submitted your application successfully, you will receive a confirmation email. We encourage you to check out our careers page often, as new opportunities become available on a regular basis.

Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion

We are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees and strive to create a diverse workplace that reflects the cultural mosaic of our great city and the communities we serve. We recognize the value that comes from different viewpoints, unique experiences and diverse perspectives of our employees, who bring fresh, new ideas to our business. Diversity plays a key role in our ability to deliver on our mission to provide clean, safe, well-maintained, affordable homes for tenants.

TCHC is committed to diversity and inclusion within its community and encourages applications from Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/persons of colour, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ+ persons, and others who can help us provide vibrant communities and make our city a great place to live. If you are a person with a disability and are experiencing issues with our job portal and would like access to our job postings in an alternative format, please email your request to our People and Culture Division at accessibility.hr@torontohousing.ca.

Accessibility for applicants

Toronto Community Housing is committed to equity in employment. Our goal is a diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free workplace that reflects the communities we serve.

We will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities at all stages of the hiring process in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code, the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005, and Toronto Community Housing’s Accessibility Policy.

If you are a person with a disability and need the job posting in an alternative format or any other accessible accommodations during the hiring process, please email your request to our People & Culture department at Accessibility.HR@torontohousing.ca or call our accessible accommodations line at (416) 981 - 4119.
